newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tequila industry fights bootleggers in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tequila industry fights bootleggers in Mexico.

text.p: After winning a battle against counterfeit tequila abroad, Mexico's tequila makers now face a battle against adulterated liquor masquerading under the same name at home, an industry spokesman said on Tuesday.

"The industry faces unfair competition from beverages sold on the domestic market calling themselves tequila, when they're not tequila," Jorge Camacho Ornelas, deputy chairman of the Tequila Chamber, told Reuters.

Camacho said the spread of tequila's popularity from traditional rough-and-ready saloons to select restaurants and drawing rooms had prompted a situation where half the tequila now sold in Mexico is phony.

Bootleg tequila, often sold at roadsides in the state of Jalisco, has spread due to the popular myth that it was made according to the original recipe and is what real macho Mexican men liked to drink, the Tequila chamber said.

Jalisco public health chief Alfredo Riebeling Guerrero told journalists on Monday that the state was stepping up its campaign to combat the sale of bootleg liquor, which can cause blindness and death.
The official response has consisted of education campaigns, confiscating illegal liquor and withdrawing brands from the market that do not conform to official standards.
Riebeling said that if confiscated liquor had a high percentage of alcohol, it was donated to hospitals for cleaning. Otherwise, it is simply disposed of, he said.
